articles.title: Festival de Gastronomia e Arte tem pratos especiais, música e exposição de carros antigos em Pirapora | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento com entrada gratuita será realizado nesta sexta-feira (9) e no sábado (10), a partir das 19h, na Orla de Pirapora.
articles.summary: Evento com entrada gratuita será realizado nesta sexta-feira (9) e no sábado (10), a partir das 19h, na Orla de Pirapora.
articles.body:
Quinze pratos fazem parte do festival — Foto: Divulgação

O município de Pirapora , no Norte de Minas, recebe neste fim de semana a terceira edição do Festival de Gastronomia e Arte, realizado pela Prefeitura em parceria com o Sebrae Minas.

Além de experimentar os pratos dos 15 estabelecimentos participantes do Prepara Gastronomia, o público poderá conferir a exposição e a comercialização de artesanatos, ações da Biblioteca Tamboril Itinerante e o III Encontro de Autos Antigos de Pirapora. A programação também inclui apresentações musicais de bandas locais nos dois dias do evento.

Com entrada gratuita, o festival será realizado na Orla de Pirapora, a partir das 19h desta sexta-feira (9) e no sábado (10).

Segundo a analista do Sebrae Minas Kátia Izabel Silva Leite, o trabalho desenvolvido com os empreendimentos do setor de alimentação contribui para valorizar a cultura alimentar e aprimorar a gestão dos negócios.

“O Festival de Gastronomia e Arte de Pirapora se consolidou e já entrou para o calendário oficial de eventos. Estes empreendimentos podem testar novas receitas e utilizar o festival como uma excelente estratégia de posicionamento de suas respectivas marcas e para o acesso a novos clientes”, destaca.

articles.title: Hayden Panettiere's daughter, 11, appears in court amid estate battle
articles.summary: Hayden Panettiere's daughter made a rare court appearance alongside her father, Wladimir Klitschko, amid a legal dispute over the actress's estate.
articles.body:
Hayden Panettiere 's daughter, Kaya , made a rare court appearance amid the legal dispute over her mother's estate.

The 11-year-old attended the Los Angeles Superior Court hearing virtually on Oct. 8 alongside her father, Wladimir Klitschko , Panettiere's former fiancé, according to The Associated Press and People . Kaya reportedly briefly appeared on camera to confirm her identity to the judge.

She was "soft-spoken and composed," People reported. The proceedings centered on Klitschko's request for "immediate" guardianship of Panettiere's estate on behalf of Kaya, the sole beneficiary, alleging "non-family members" have been misappropriating the "Nashville" star's property.

The judge ultimately granted Klitschko temporary guardianship of the estate and set another court date for Dec. 7, noting Kaya would not need to be present.

Hayden Panettiere and Wladimir Klitschko's lasting connection – See photos

Hayden Panettiere, 36, died after suffering cardiac arrest in Greenville, South Carolina . Her ex-fiancé, boxer Wladimir Klitschko, is speaking out about their family's profound shock and grief following the announcement of her death. Klitschko, who holds full custody of their daughter, Kaya, wrote that while Panettiere was "no longer" his partner, she played "an important part" in his life. Look back at their relationship in photos. Here Pannettier stands with Klitschko as he waves to fans after losing the fight against Tyson Fury on Nov. 28, 2015 in Esprit Arena, Dusseldorf, Germany. Klitschko's 11-year reign as heavyweight champion ended that night.

Wladimir Klitschko alleges Hayden Panettiere's estate is at risk

Panettiere met Klitschko in 2009. The couple were engaged in 2013 and welcomed Kaya the following year before splitting in 2018. The former boxing champion later obtained full custody.

Panettiere died Aug. 16 at age 36. The Greenville County Coroner's Office ruled that her death resulted from the "toxic effects of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, Alprazolam, Methocarbamol and Quetiapine."

Klitschko filed his petition for temporary guardianship of the estate on Sept. 24, stating he "is informed and believes that non-family members previously connected to Hayden have accessed and destroyed Hayden's emails" and "certain items of personal property belonging to Hayden, including jewelry, have disappeared or remain unaccounted for," according to documents previously obtained by USA TODAY.

The filing said his appointment was "urgent and essential" so he could have "the necessary standing to file Hayden's probate petition, and the power to nominate a proposed administrator of Hayden's Estate." Without Klitschko in that position, the petition alleged, there is a "high probability that property belonging to Hayden's estate may be lost, damaged or dissipated before a duly appointed personal representative can be in place to protect it."

Amid the investigation into Panettiere's death, federal agents have accessed her Los Angeles home "and removed property," according to Klitschko. But there is currently no one "authorized to safeguard the interests of Hayden's estate in connection with the investigation, including the return of estate property once it is no longer needed by investigators, and to interface with investigators on behalf of Haden's estate."

The filing further alleged that Panettiere hired a security service to protect her home due to "a documented concern that an individual had gained unauthorized access to Hayden's property." After she died, the home's locks were allegedly changed and her "designer clothing and accessories worn to public appearances have been relocated as a precaution."

Still, the petition added that "it is expected that the individual will continue to try and misappropriate property belonging to Hayden's Estate."

During the Oct. 8 hearing, Klitschko's lawyers reportedly said he will use his power as temporary guardian to "request" and "authorize" law enforcement to investigate and aid in the recovery of the misappropriated property.

articles.title: Dakota Johnson habla sobre su destape integral más vergonzoso: "Lo dejé crecer"
articles.standfirst: En plena promoción de 'Verity' desempolva su pasado con '50 sombras de Grey'
articles.summary: En plena promoción de 'Verity' desempolva su pasado con '50 sombras de Grey'
articles.body: Dakota Johnson está en plena promoción de su nueva película, Verity, y la actriz ha vuelto a dejar una anécdota relacionada con otras interpretaciones que causaron un shock en el ámbito cinematográfico. La actriz que reparte su papel junto a Anne Hathaway y Josh Hartnett, participó en un divertido reto para el canal de YouTube First We Feast. Allí tuvo que elegir entre responder a una pregunta comprometida o enfrentarse a preguntas picantes... La intérprete no se lo pensó dos veces. Aceptó. La cuestión era sencilla: revelar lo más vergonzoso que había hecho para preparar un personaje. Su respuesta desató las risas inmediatas de sus compañeros. En un primer momento, la actriz bromeó asegurando que había sido para Madame Web, aunque enseguida aclaró que en realidad se trataba de la primera entrega de 50 sombras de Grey. "Fue para la primera película. Había una escena de desnudo integral y se suponía que mi personaje nunca se había depilado", desveló Johnson entre risas. La confesión provocó la curiosidad de Anne Hathaway, que le preguntó si no había considerado utilizar una prótesis capilar utilizada habitualmente en cine para este tipo de escenas. La respuesta de Johnson fue tan breve como contundente: "No". Pese a haber participado después en films tan destacados como Suspiria, La hija oscura o Materialistas, Dakota Johnson sigue acumulando titulares vinculados a la saga que la convirtió en una estrella mundial. Y esta última confesión demuestra que el rodaje de 50 sombras de Grey todavía guarda historias capaces de sorprender al público. Johnson también estuvo en el popular programa Saturday Night Live y en él confesó que la película "es un thriller erótico psico-sexual y, ¿sabéis qué? Salir con músicos también lo es", para añadir: “Algunos no llevan zapatos, algunos son terribles en la cama, pero todos están en mi buzón de mensajes privados. Aunque es culpa mía. Algunas personas salen de los conciertos con merchandising y yo salgo de los conciertos con una relación de dos años y medio”, en alusión a cómo comenzó su relación en concreto con Chris Martin.

articles.title: 'Drishyam 3' box office collection day 8 (LIVE): Ajay Devgn, Jaideep Ahlawat's film crosses Rs 257 crore net in India, sees drop on second Friday
articles.summary: ‘Drishyam 3: The Conclusion’ has continued its impressive run at the Indian box office, closing its opening week on a strong note in the crime thriller
articles.body: ‘Drishyam 3: The Conclusion’ has continued its impressive run at the Indian box office, closing its opening week on a strong note in the crime thriller genre. After registering substantial collections over the first weekend, the film sustained its momentum through the weekdays. With its second weekend underway, the Ajay Devgn-starrer is witnessing encouraging advance bookings for its second Friday and is on track to record the second-highest second-Friday collection for a Bollywood film in 2026, behind ‘Dhurandhar 2’.The film has also retained a strong screen presence in its second week. Despite fresh releases entering cinemas, ‘Drishyam 3: The Conclusion’ began its second week with 15,017 shows across India, a drop of just 1,471 shows from the 16,488 screenings it had on day 7. The makers have also continued with blockbuster ticket pricing, although rates have been marginally reduced compared to the opening weekend.With this, 'Drishyam 3' has wrapped up its first week with Rs 245 crore net.On Friday, day 8, the film has made Rs 11.73 crore till evening. The total collection now stands at Rs 257.23 crore net in India. articles.title: Crazy Rich Asians TV show to reunite Constance Wu and Henry Golding
articles.summary: It will pick up after the hit 2018 film, starring Constance Wu, Henry Golding, Michelle Yeoh and Ronny Chieng.
articles.body:
Four of the stars of 2018's Crazy Rich Asians film are reprising their roles for a TV show of the same name.

The series will pick up events after the end of the hit film, with Constance Wu and Henry Golding playing their lead roles of Rachel and Nick, while Ronny Chieng is back as Eddie and Oscar winner Michelle Yeoh will have a recurring role as Nick's mother Eleanor.

"It's a 'Crazy Rich' family reunion!" said Adele Lim, who co-wrote the film, calling it the sequel we've been waiting for". It will "delve into the characters and worlds of Kevin Kwan's brilliant books" over eight episodes, she said.

The show will be made by HBO, and the news was announced days after HBO's parent company Warner Bros announced its £110bn (£82.8bn) merger with Paramount Skydance .

Adapted from Kwan's bestseller books, written between 2013 and 2017, the film topped the US box office and was nominated for two Golden Globes.

It featured an all-Asian cast and told the story of an Asian-American woman who gets a culture shock meeting her boyfriend's ultra-wealthy family in Singapore.

Lim is showrunner for the new TV series and will be one of the executive producers, as will the the film's director Jon M Chu.

He said the film had "changed his life", calling the cast and crew the "most creative and hilarious group of people I've ever known".

"Since then, this cast has become movie stars, superheroes, arena-filling performers and even an Oscar winner, so bringing everyone back together feels like coming home."

Lim added: "Our writers room is humming and we can't wait to share what we've come up with."

The series, co-produced by HBO and Warner Bros Television, will start production next year.

"Constance, Henry, Ronny, and Michelle are global superstars, and we know the passionate fans of the film and megahit novels can't wait to see more," said said Casey Bloys, co-chair and chief content officer of Skydance Direct-To-Consumer.

articles.title: When Katrina Kaif revealed how Nana Patekar helped her deliver a big dialogue scene in 'Raajneeti': 'It's going to be fine'
articles.summary: An old interview of Katrina Kaif has resurfaced online, in which she spoke about how veteran actor Nana Patekar helped her stay composed while shooting a
articles.body: An old interview of Katrina Kaif has resurfaced online, in which she spoke about how veteran actor Nana Patekar helped her stay composed while shooting a key speech scene for Prakash Jha’s ‘Rajneeti’. The film featured a large ensemble cast.Katrina Kaif’s nervous moment on setIn the film, Katrina Kaif had to address a huge gathering. She described the experience in a conversation with Mid Day. She had said, "There were 2000-3000 people on the street. They were not extras. I had to walk onto the stage and deliver a speech. Ajay (Devgn), Nana Sir were there. My hands were trembling. I remember Nana sir saying, it’s fine. It’s going to be fine."Her role as Indu PratapKatrina Kaif played Indu Pratap, who eventually becomes the Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh. Her character is in love with the role played by Ranbir Kapoor but is married to his brother, Prithviraj Pratap, played by Arjun Rampal. Reports suggest the character was inspired by Draupadi from the Mahabharat.Nana Patekar’s part in the filmNana Patekar appeared as Brij Gopal, a sharp political strategist who guides the family’s moves in the story.Last rites of the veteran actorAccording to reports, Nana Patekar was found unconscious at his home in Dona Paula, Goa, and was taken to Manipal Hospital. Doctors tried to revive him for nearly 45 minutes before declaring him dead.His last rites were performed at the Donje farmhouse in Pune on Thursday with full state honours. The atmosphere echoed with chants of "Nana Amar Rahe" (Long Live Nana). His associates said he had expressed a wish to be cremated at his farmhouse.More about 'Rajneeti'Directed by Prakash Jha, the cast of the film featured Ajay Devgn, Nana Patekar, Ranbir Kapoor, Katrina Kaif, Arjun Rampal, Manoj Bajpayee, Sarah Thompson and Naseeruddin Shah. articles.title: Lamine Yamal se estrena como diseñador con una colección compuesta por 29 prendas: "Refleja quién soy y cómo me gusta vestir"
articles.standfirst: El futbolista se ha aliado con American Eagle para lanzar su primera colección de moda: 'American Eagle x Lamine Yamal'
articles.summary: El futbolista se ha aliado con American Eagle para lanzar su primera colección de moda: 'American Eagle x Lamine Yamal'
articles.body: El futbolista Lamine Yamal ha llevado su estilo más allá del terreno de juego con la presentación en Barcelona de su primera colección exclusiva junto a American Eagle: 'American Eagle x Lamine Yamal'. La marca estadounidense ha convertido durante 48 horas distintos espacios de la Ciudad Condal en escenarios de una celebración que ha unido moda, música, arte urbano y cultura juvenil para acercar a sus seguidores las 29 prendas diseñadas en colaboración con el jugador del Barça. La iniciativa ha supuesto la primera activación de American Eagle en España y ha formado parte de la estrategia de la compañía para ampliar su presencia y relevancia cultural en Europa. La colección, que se lanzó el mes pasado, ya está disponible a través de la tienda 'online' de la marca. Uno de los principales puntos de encuentro ha sido 'The Studio', un espacio 'pop-up' situado en la Dreta de l’Eixample donde los artistas locales Urees, Otti Hats, Ugo Boulard y Düa Düa impartieron talleres gratuitos de personalización de prendas vaqueras. Los asistentes han podido experimentar con el denim y dar un toque propio a sus prendas, en línea con la apuesta de la colección por la expresión individual. La propuesta también ha llegado al arte urbano con un nuevo mural de 21 metros de altura dedicado a Lamine Yamal y a su colaboración con American Eagle. La obra, creada por el artista TV Boy, se ha convertido en otro de los elementos destacados de la intervención en la ciudad. La celebración ha culminado en el 'American Eagle Beach Club', situado en la playa de Moll de la Marina, donde Lamine Yamal ha hecho una aparición sorpresa. Allí ha ejercido de jurado en una batalla de rap ante cientos de invitados, en un evento que combinó música y cultura urbana. Lamine Yamal se ha mostrado satisfecho con la acogida de la iniciativa y con la posibilidad de compartir el proyecto con su ciudad. "Es muy especial ver cómo mi colección con American Eagle cobra vida aquí, en Barcelona, y cómo la gente hace suyas las prendas", ha declarado el delantero azulgrana, quien también ha destacado su vínculo personal con la moda: "La moda es algo que siempre me ha gustado, y esta colección refleja quién soy y cómo me gusta vestir. Poder compartirla con mi ciudad lo hace aún más especial". Por su parte, Craig Brommers, director de Marketing de American Eagle, ha subrayado la conexión del deportista con las nuevas generaciones y su capacidad para representar los valores de la marca. Según ha exlicado, la colaboración busca unir denim, música, creatividad y cultura juvenil para acercar American Eagle a nuevos consumidores europeos a través de experiencias vinculadas al entorno del futbolista. La colección 'American Eagle x Lamine Yamal', compuesta por 29 prendas, ya se puede adquirir en el sitio web en Europa de la firma estadounidense, en Con esta colaboración, la marca refuerza su apuesta por vincular la moda con figuras del deporte y referentes culturales capaces de conectar con el público joven.

articles.title: In 2025, Mandy Moore found refuge at Hilary Duff’s Beverly Hills home amid Los Angeles wildfires
articles.summary: In January 2025, Mandy Moore sought refuge in Hilary Duff's Beverly Hills home after wildfires devastated her Altadena residence. Both families showed incredible support during the crisis, highlighting the strength of their long-standing friendship.
articles.body: When the devastating Los Angeles wildfires forced Mandy Moore and her family to leave their Altadena home, they found a temporary place to stay with someone they already knew well. Hilary Duff and her husband, Matthew Koma, opened their Beverly Hills home to Moore, her husband Taylor Goldsmith and their three children as the family dealt with the aftermath of the Eaton Fire.The arrangement was revealed by Moore's brother-in-law, Griffin Goldsmith, who also lost his own home in the fires. In an Instagram post shared during the crisis, Griffin thanked Duff and Koma for taking care of his brother's family and for helping his own family through the disaster. People described the gesture as the couple taking in Moore's family after their home was impacted by the fires.How did Mandy Moore's family end up leaving their Altadena home?Moore and Goldsmith had built a family life in Altadena, where they lived with their three children. When the Eaton Fire reached the area in January 2025, the family evacuated with their children and pets.In an Instagram update shared after the evacuation, Mandy Moore explained that the main part of their house was still standing but was unsafe to live in. She also said the garage, home studio and back house had been destroyed, while homes belonging to relatives, friends and neighbours were lost. E! News reported the same details from Moore's social media updates.The situation meant that the family needed somewhere to stay while they figured out what came next. That was when Hilary Duff and Matthew Koma stepped in.Hilary Duff turned her Beverly Hills home into a temporary refugeDuff and Koma offered their Beverly Hills house to Moore, Goldsmith and their children. Griffin Goldsmith publicly expressed his gratitude to the couple, saying they supported his family from the beginning of the crisis.The gesture was especially meaningful because the two actresses have known each other for more than two decades. Architectural Digest noted that Mandy Moore and Hilary Duff had both become well-known young stars in the early 2000s and had remained close as their lives changed and both became mothers.Duff's husband also helped organise a GoFundMe campaign for Griffin and his wife, Kit, whose own home had been destroyed. The fundraiser was intended to help them begin rebuilding after the loss.Inside the Beverly Hills home where Moore's family stayedDuff had a 5,260-square-foot Georgian-style Beverly Hills house that she had transformed into a private family home, according to Architectural Digest. Duff purchased the house after looking for a more secluded place to live. She told the magazine that she liked the feeling of being tucked away from the busy Los Angeles surroundings, describing the property as feeling like a "warm hug."The home had undergone major renovations over the years. Duff worked with designers including David Ko of Maison Ko and the team behind Studio Life/Style to make the interiors brighter and more suitable for family life.That same family-friendly quality became especially relevant when Mandy Moore and her children needed somewhere safe to stay.A friendship that goes beyond HollywoodThe connection between Mandy Moore and Hilary Duff was not simply one between two actors who happened to know each other.The two had remained part of the same social circle as their careers developed and their families grew. Duff had spoken about their close group of mothers and the time they spent together with their children.During the fires, that long friendship took on a very different meaning. Moore's family was dealing with the uncertainty of having a home that could no longer safely accommodate them, while Duff and Koma were able to provide a place where the family could stay.For Moore, the situation was also complicated by the wider loss around her. Her brother-in-law and others close to the family had lost their homes, while much of their Altadena neighbourhood had been badly affected.What happened to Mandy Moore's home later?The damage to Moore's property did not mean the entire house had to be rebuilt from scratch.In a 2026 AD follow-up, Moore and Goldsmith revealed that they had eventually returned to their Altadena home after months of restoration work. The main structure had survived the fire, but smoke damage meant that extensive remediation was necessary.The couple replaced damaged materials, including clothing, textiles and furniture, and undertook work on the home's walls, ductwork and HVAC system before it was considered safe for their children.Their return marked a very different chapter from the early days of the disaster, when Duff's Beverly Hills home had provided a temporary place for the family.From a Hollywood friendship to a real act of supportThe story of Mandy Moore and Hilary Duff during the Los Angeles wildfires became less about celebrity homes and more about what people do for one another when circumstances suddenly change.Moore's family had to leave a house they had spent years making into a home. Duff and Matthew Koma responded by opening their own doors, while also helping another family affected by the fires.Years later, Moore and Goldsmith were able to return to their Altadena home. But for a difficult period when their own house was not safe to live in, Duff's Beverly Hills residence became a temporary home for the family.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Amitabh Bachchan pays tribute to Nana Patekar with throwback videos, including the late actor singing 'Main Zindagi Ka Saath Nibhata Chala'
articles.summary: Amitabh Bachchan has paid an emotional tribute to Nana Patekar, who died on Thursday morning.
articles.body: Amitabh Bachchan has paid an emotional tribute to Nana Patekar, who died on Thursday morning. The megastar posted throwback videos of the late actor on Instagram, recalling his special moments on ‘Kaun Banega Crorepati’.Amitabh Bachchan’s Instagram tributeOne of the clips shows Nana talking about shooting an episode of ‘Kaun Banega Crorepati’ with Big B, taken from an interview with NDTV. Another video shows him singing ‘Main Zindagi Ka Saath Nibhata Chala’ while sitting on the KBC hot seat. Amitabh also shared the same videos on his Instagram stories.How Nana Patekar diedNana suffered a severe cardiac arrest at his home in Goa. Reports say he felt uneasy in the early hours and called a friend, after which he was taken to Manipal Hospital. Doctors reportedly tried to revive him for around 45 minutes.Journey to PuneHis mortal remains were then taken to Pune. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis paid his respects at the airport. The body was later taken by road to the family farmhouse in Donje village.Funeral with state honoursPolitical leaders, film personalities and more than 1,000 admirers attended the last rites. His body was draped in the Tricolour, and a marching band walked with the procession. Female police officers fired a 21-gun salute. Many fans had reached the venue in the afternoon and waited for hours. Chants of “Nana Patekar amar rahe!” rang out as people said their final goodbye.Who attendedThose present included Maharashtra Deputy Chief Ministers Eknath Shinde and Sunetra Pawar, Union Ministers Murlidhar Mohol and Ramdas Athawale, and state ministers Chandrakant Patil, Uday Samant and Madhuri Misal. Actors Jackie Shroff, Pravin Tarde and Kiran Yadnyopavit were also there.Arrangements for the crowdTo handle the big gathering, organisers set up a raised platform for the funeral pyre, a tent for dignitaries, barricades for crowd control and a large screen for the public. Several shops and establishments in and around Khadakwasla stayed shut to allow the procession to pass smoothly.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: James Bond legend Roger Moore's son calls out TikTok culture, Hollywood's recycled comic book movies
articles.summary: Geoffrey Moore stars in spy thriller "Knightfall" and shares why Hollywood needs stronger stories over big-budget spectacle and recycled comics.
articles.body: Forget bigger explosions — Geoffrey Moore says Hollywood needs better stories. The son of the late James Bond legend Roger Moore told Fox News Digital that today’s films have become too reliant on recycled comic book material and big-budget spectacle, while originality and meaningful dialogue have taken a back seat. "I think that today, it's too much TikTok," the actor told Fox News Digital. "A person will have a conversation with you, and it's the conversation that he read or heard on TikTok, as opposed to actually having read Hemingway and knows what he's talking about." GABRIEL BASSO SAYS SOCIAL MEDIA HAS TURNED PEOPLE INTO VOYEURS OBSESSED WITH STRANGERS' LIVES: 'IT'S WEIRD' "I think it's important that the art of storytelling maintains the culture," Moore said. "There's just too many studio executive heads deciding what's right, as opposed to what people want to hear or people should hear and see." Moore stars in the British spy thriller "Knightfall," which has its share of guns and fight scenes. However, he said the film doesn't rely on over-the-top action to keep audiences hooked and instead leans on a strong storyline and sharp dialogue. "I would like to see more culture in films, as opposed to the regurgitation of these comics," Moore said. WATCH: BOND GIRL ALISON PAPWORTH REVEALS HER HOPE FOR THE NEXT 007 "And everything's so negative. Oh, my goodness. It's like, you need to have a certain budget with helicopters flying upside down. But the storyline has to be strong. Good dialogue, good storywriting are key. You don't have to have constant action to keep the person's attention going. You also need action in the storyline, in the words." Moore also believes "Knightfall" has something else working in its favor in the social media era: It doesn't overstay its welcome. The actor said the film was deliberately kept short, acknowledging that today's audiences may not have the patience to sit through a lengthy saga. "You can't sit through a three-hour movie," he argued. "You can imagine today, it's just everyone on the treadmill. You need that right amount of length before someone starts asking, 'When is it over?' That's the direction I would take with today's films." For Moore, "Knightfall" also marks a full-circle moment. The actor grew up immersed in the entertainment business as the son of one of Hollywood's most famous spies. Now, decades later, he's stepping in front of the camera as a spy himself at roughly the same age his father was when he made his final James Bond film. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE "I have not been an actor all my life, even though I did start as a child actor," Moore said. "My second womb was the soundstage. But just because you're related to someone in the entertainment industry, it doesn't make me a part of the entertainment industry or even an actor. But this time, it just felt right. It wasn't forced. And also, it's never too late. I mean, yes, go figure, it's a spy film, but there's a twist. And really, it's never too late." Moore was six years old when his father filmed his 007 debut, "Live and Let Die," which was released in 1973. The Telegraph reported that Moore was present for all of his father's Bond films and the famous stunts that came with them. Once the director yelled "cut," the patriarch would look at his son and ask if he wanted to get ice cream. "Look, I've been on enough film sets to know how laborious it can be," Moore said. "It's a demanding schedule and you mustn't break your ankle. But I've never had a big role where I'm doing a lot of running around. I have to say on some mornings when I wake up, if you've ever been horseback riding, you recognize muscles you never knew you had. I'm doing all of this running around and going, 'Oh my goodness, I thought I was fit!'" "I was never like, 'I'm looking for a job in front of the camera,'" Moore continued. "It just felt right. And I was intrigued. It's an independent British film and very few films aren't dictated by executive heads. This isn't a regurgitation of another franchise where they're spending lots of money. Here, the conditions were harsh. It was physically demanding. Rewrites are happening on the day. It was back to back." "The food was good, considering this wasn't a multimillion production," he said. "And if the money is good, that'll get your attention." Moore said the key to making it in the movie-making business is simple: don't take yourself too seriously. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "If an actor shows up on the set and doesn't understand the importance of the production, what each person does, then they're in the wrong business," he said. "It's a team effort. Everyone is as important. You're nothing without the guy who knows how to keep you in focus. If you make something look good, it's usually not that easy. And to be a film star, you have to be a good actor. There's no such thing as an ignorant person who can act." Despite following in his father's footsteps by playing a spy, Moore isn't campaigning to become the next James Bond. "I think the next James Bond should be someone who can carry the decade, a reflection of the times," Moore said. "When it comes to who's the next Bond, it's really who depicts the times, who is relevant to today, whether it be a tall person, a short person, someone who doesn't know how to tie a tie or who doesn't know how to read because he's on TikTok the whole time. Who knows who they'll choose." "I think they know what they'll be doing. They're not just handing it over to Amazon, that was basically a delivery service, and now they're in the film business. Who they ultimately choose is someone relevant to the times. And I think that's the key to Bond." Amazon MGM Studios gained creative control of the James Bond franchise in 2025 after forming a joint venture with longtime Bond producers Michael G. Wilson and Barbara Broccoli. The transaction closed March 24, 2025, with Amazon MGM Studios, Wilson and Broccoli remaining co-owners of the franchise. Several actors have been linked to the role, including Paul Mescal, Jacob Elordi, Jack O'Connell, Jack Lowden and Callum Turner. PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE The next installment will be the 26th film in the official Bond series, which began with "Dr. No" in 1962. Denis Villeneuve is set to direct, with "Peaky Blinders" creator Steven Knight writing the screenplay. As Moore looks ahead to making more films, there's one piece of advice from his late father, who died in 2017 at age 89, that he hasn't forgotten. "Make sure you get paid," he joked. articles.title: Zachary Levi says Texas gives him the ‘freedom’ he couldn’t find in California
articles.summary: Zachary Levi says he traded California for Texas "freedom" and values that are "more aligned with mine." The actor is starring in the new Western remake "Angel and the Badman."
articles.body: Zachary Levi believes Texas offered him the kind of freedom and shared values that he no longer felt he had in his home state of California. In 2017, the 45-year-old actor, who is starring in the new Western movie "Angel and the Badman," left Los Angeles behind and moved to a ranch outside Austin. During a recent interview with Fox News Digital alongside his "Angel and the Badman" co-stars, Neal McDonough and Meg Fraser, as well as the film's director, Julio Quintana, Levi reflected on trading the Golden State for the Lone Star State, noting that the "great state of Texas" is a "much easier place to live than a lot of the other places that I have lived." 'FRIDAY NIGHT LIGHTS' STAR ADRIANNE PALICKI SAYS TEXAS GAVE HER SOMETHING HOLLYWOOD COULDN'T "I love California. It's a beautiful state," he said. "Unfortunately, I think it's got a lot of issues and I don't see those going anywhere." "Whereas in Texas, I think that their values are more aligned with mine," he continued. "I appreciate that I don't have to pay state income tax and there's liberty. There's the liberty to go do what I want to go do, which is, like, go buy a bunch of land and build a movie studio." NEWSOM SAYS FILM TAX INCENTIVES ARE BRINGING HOLLYWOOD HOME BUT INDUSTRY EXPERTS WARN IT MAY BE 'TOO LATE' "You can be a crazy person and go do that," Levi added. "If Walt Disney tried to go build Disneyland in California today, I don't think it would ever get done, you know, so it gives me the freedom to go live the life that I believe that I'm meant to go live." Levi is currently building Wyldwood Studios, a $100 million film and lifestyle campus on his 75-acre property in Bastrop County outside Austin. Designed as a hybrid production hub and creative retreat, the multiphase project pairs soundstages and production offices with housing and wellness spaces. Wyldwood is expected to open its first two soundstages in 2027. WATCH: ZACHARY LEVI SAYS TEXAS GAVE HIM THE FREEDOM HE COULDN'T FIND IN CALIFORNIA The "Chuck" alum previously told Fox News Digital that the inspiration to build Wyldwood was rooted in his longstanding desire to rethink how the entertainment industry operates from the inside out. "Ever since I started working in Hollywood and I saw how broken it all was, I felt very compelled by God to go build a better Hollywood — like a new United Artists kind of studio — where it's owned and operated by the artists, where we can cut out all the middlemen, where we all can do really well, build a community," Levi said. "And then not just a place to work," he continued. "People can live there, and kids can go to school there. And we have an organic farm, and, like, all of the things that I think everybody really wants these days." Levi's latest project, "Angel and the Badman," which was produced by Angel Studios, is a remake of the classic 1947 Western of the same name that starred John Wayne, Gail Russell, Harry Carey and Bruce Cabot. The official plot synopsis for the remake reads, "When feared outlaw Quirt Evans staggers onto a rancher's land with a bullet in his back, he expects a quick death, not mercy. But Penny, the rancher's daughter, offers him a chance at something he’s never had: a life beyond violence. However, the past doesn’t forgive. With the marshal closing in and an outlaw gang ready to burn the ranch to the ground, Quirt must decide what kind of man he’ll be when the world demands blood." Levi stepped into Wayne's original role as Quirt Evans (the Badman) while Fraser plays Penny (the Angel) and McDonough portrays the marshal. "Angel and the Badman" also stars Tommy Lee Jones as the outlaw gang leader Laredo. WATCH: NEAL MCDONOUGH SAYS YOUNG PEOPLE NEED TO SEE ‘THE BAD GUY GETS WHAT HE DESERVES’ While speaking with Fox News Digital, McDonough explained how he believes "Angel and the Badman" conveys an important message for the young people of today. "I think nowadays — with the temptation of social media and what we look at and what we hear and what we listen to — who do we look up to as heroes anymore?" he said. "Especially for the younger generation, it's really hard for them." "The younger generation who don't really know Westerns so well, to go to a film like ‘Angel and the Badman,’ you see, ‘OK, the bad guy gets what he deserves in the end,’" McDonough continued. "Where in modern day, the bad guy sometimes gets to go scot-free and that's tough to really learn from as a kid. What do you learn from that as a young adult?" "So films like this are important because it tells us, you should be trying to do the right thing," he added. "You should redeem yourself and not do the dumb things that you used to do. Try to be a better person, try to give glory to Him, try and do the right thing for your family. I love doing films like these because they do exactly that, and thank goodness for Angel Studios." Quintana said he believed that the story’s redemptive themes feel especially relevant in a social media era when public mistakes can quickly become permanent scandals. "In modern culture, in some ways, we actually have the inverse situation where it seems like we're always — you make one public mistake, and it's like your life is ruined," he said. "Our media outlets thrive on downfall and self-destruction and things like that. And I think this is a good reminder that actually what's really inspiring is people making mistakes and ultimately making the sacrifices to make amends and try to claw their way back up and try to be better, because we don't really see the redemptive side of a public downfall. Nowadays, we only see the dark side." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE McDonough shared that he personally resonates with redemptive storytelling after his past struggles with substance abuse issues. During a 2025 interview with Fox News Digital, the "Band of Brothers" star explained that he gave up alcohol in 2016 after realizing he had to make his life about serving God, "rather than serving me." He also credited his wife of over 22 years, Ruvé, with giving him the motivation he needed to quit drinking as he recalled, "She grabbed me and says, it's us or the bottle, you choose," and he "never looked back." Reflecting on "Angel and the Badman's" message of redemption, McDonough admitted, "I think that we all do things that we are not proud of at times." WATCH: ‘ANGEL AND THE BADMAN’ STAR ZACHARY LEVI SAYS REDEMPTION STORIES APPLY TO EVERYONE "We all make mistakes," he continued. "None of us are perfect. We all sin, we all do dumb things, but every once in a while, you get called out and something might happen to make you think, ‘Hmm, maybe I should be a better dad. Maybe I should be a better husband. Maybe I should be better coworker. I need to stop doing that thing.’" "Years ago, I stopped drinking because it took me off my game, and it just wasn't keeping me focused to do His work," McDonough remembered. "And ever since then, I focused so hard on doing His work and giving glory to Him and everything that I do. So we all have to overcome these things and that's redemption. And ‘Angel and the Badman,’ boy, you know, Quirt Evans has to go through that." "It's that redemptive quality that Westerns have more than any other films," he added. "They keep it simple. There's a good guy, there's a bad guy. Good guy's gonna win, but he has to overcome something because the bad guy couldn't. And that's what we did in ‘Angel and the Badman.’" LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS Levi told Fox News Digital that he also believed that the movie's message was universal. PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE "I love a good redemption story," he said. "It's one of the most classic stories that you can tell, and if you can tell it within a classic genre like a Western that has a little bit of all of these subcategories of action-adventure and romance and drama and comedy and heart and charm and all of those things woven into one beautifully shot and directed story — then you get to tell a story that I believe applies to everyone." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Because everyone knows deep down inside of them, they either have been redeemed or are in need of redemption," Levi continued. "It's a human story. It's a human story. So those are the ones that I like to tell the most."

articles.title: In 2023, Heather Dubrow bought a Beverly Hills mansion for $16 million; renovations pushed the projected cost to $32 million
articles.summary: Explore the expensive journey of Heather Dubrow as she navigates her ambitious $32 million renovation of a Beverly Hills mansion purchased for $16 million. Learn about the challenges, financial burdens, and the eventual sale of this dream home gone wrong.
articles.body: For Heather Dubrow, buying a Beverly Hills mansion was supposed to be another dream house project. She and her husband, Dr. Terry Dubrow, had already built and sold their famous Orange County home, so their next property was meant to be something special too.They bought the Beverly Hills estate in 2023 for around $16 million. Then came the renovation plans. Heather wanted to take the house “down to the studs,” and the projected all-in cost eventually reached around $32 million. What looked like an exciting new chapter slowly turned into a very expensive headache.Heather Dubrow bought the Beverly Hills estate for $16.1 million in 2023On 24 July 2023, Entertainment Tonight reported that Heather and Terry Dubrow had bought the Beverly Hills property for $16.1 million, well below its original $37.5 million asking price. Heather herself confirmed the purchase to ET and called it an “iconic, Hollywood estate.”The estate had a serious Hollywood connection. It had previously belonged to legendary film producer Dino De Laurentiis and his wife, producer Martha De Laurentiis. The property sits in the Beverly Hills Post Office area, at the end of a long gated driveway.The estate also gave the Dubrows plenty to work with. It had expansive grounds, a swimming pool, a tennis court, multiple living spaces and views stretching across Los Angeles.Heather Dubrow wanted to completely transform the Beverly Hills mansionThe house was never supposed to stay the way they bought it. During the Season 18 premiere of 'The Real Housewives of Orange County' on 11 July 2024, Heather Dubrow explained just how ambitious the renovation was. She said they were going to take the house “down to the studs,” essentially stripping it back before rebuilding it around her vision.But there was a slightly funny reality to all that planning: they were already living in the house while figuring everything out.Heather showed viewers rooms with temporary furniture and even a refrigerator marked “do not open.” She joked about how strange it was to be living in the middle of a future construction site.Heather Dubrow's $32 million renovation was a projection, not a final billThis is where the numbers around the Beverly Hills mansion can get confusing. The $32 million figure was a projected running total, not an amount Heather and Terry Dubrow were confirmed to have spent.In the July 2024 episode, the couple's renovation planning estimated that they could spend around $2 million to $3 million on landscaping, more than $2 million on the guest house and another $1 million on a movie theater. Along with the other work, that pushed the projected total cost of the property to around $32 million.Heather Dubrow later spoke directly to Bravo on 6 August 2024 about the project, describing the house as very different from her previous homes. At that stage, the estimated running total was still around $32 million.So, technically, Heather and Terry did not buy a $32 million house. They bought it for roughly $16 million and were looking at a potential $32 million all-in cost after the planned renovation.Heather Dubrow's dream renovation turned into a financial burdenThe renovation became much more complicated than Heather Dubrow had expected. By the time the Dubrows were discussing the project again on 'RHOC', the house had become a major source of stress. Heather later described the construction as a “disaster,” while the couple faced delays, rising costs and major work on the property.The situation became even more complicated when asbestos was discovered during the renovation. Heather also revealed that the contractor had gone significantly over the budget they had originally agreed upon. What was meant to be a dream home was now a house that required even more time and money.Heather Dubrow eventually sold the Beverly Hills mansion for $16.5 millionBy 2025, the Dubrows decided it was time to let the property go. The Beverly Hills estate was listed for $25 million in March 2025 and was later reduced to just under $20 million. The property ultimately sold for $16.5 million in August 2025, according to The Real Deal's contemporaneous report on the transaction.Heather Dubrow later admitted that walking away from the project was difficult. In Bravo's coverage of the sale, she described it as a project she had once seen as her dream house but eventually realised was not viable for the family anymore.And that is what makes the Beverly Hills mansion story so striking. Heather Dubrow went into the deal thinking she had found another home to put her personal stamp on. Instead, a roughly $16 million purchase came with a projected $32 million renovation, construction problems and a $16.5 million sale two years later.Sometimes, even in Beverly Hills, the dream house is the one you eventually decide to leave behind.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: MC PH é entrevistado no g1 Ouviu ao vivo desta quarta-feira (14)
articles.summary: Cantor é o convidado do podcast de música do g1, com transmissão ao vivo no g1, no YouTube e no TikTok.
articles.body:
Cantor é o convidado do podcast de música do g1, com transmissão ao vivo no g1, no YouTube e no TikTok.

MC PH será entrevistado ao vivo no g1 Ouviu, o podcast e videocast de música do g1, nesta quarta-feira (14), a partir das 11h30. A conversa ficará disponível em vídeo e podcast no g1, no YouTube, no TikTok e nas plataformas de áudio.

PH chegou como aposta promissora no trap funk em 2023 e hoje já é um dos principais nomes da música urbana nacional. Em agosto, o artista lançou “A era de ouro”, um álbum de estúdio com 13 faixas e focado nas raízes do funk paulista. “Eu sempre fiz música a partir da minha realidade, mas agora é maior que isso. É sobre representar o Brasil inteiro, mostrar nossa força e nossa estética do nosso jeito”, contou PH ao lançar o projeto.

Ouça as edições anteriores do g1 Ouviu: O podcast traz personagens da música que falam sobre carreira, desafios, composições e histórias de vida.

articles.title: At 13, Jason Weaver was offered $2 million by Disney to sing as young Simba in The Lion King; his mother chose $100,000 plus royalties instead, and 32 years later he says the checks are still coming
articles.summary: At 13, most children are still figuring out what they want to be when they grow up.
articles.body: At 13, most children are still figuring out what they want to be when they grow up. For Jason Weaver, however, life had already presented an opportunity that could have changed his family's fortunes overnight. When Disney offered him $2 million to lend his voice to young Simba in The Lion King, it was the kind of money most teenagers could only dream of. But his mother and manager, Marilyn “Kitty” Haywood, saw something beyond the staggering figure. She turned down the lump-sum offer, negotiated an upfront payment of around $100,000 and royalties instead, and made a decision that Weaver says continues to pay off more than three decades later.Now 47, the actor and singer has revealed how his mother's foresight helped him build a lasting source of income from one of Disney's most successful animated films. Recalling the deal in a 2019 interview with VladTV, which has recently resurfaced on social media, Weaver said the original offer was essentially designed to pay him once and close the matter.“When they offered that deal, it was really just to take this money and go,” he recalled, suggesting that Disney already anticipated the enormous commercial potential of the film.For a family from Chicago, $2 million in the early 1990s was no small amount. Weaver had already experienced success, including playing a young Michael Jackson, for which he said his biggest cheque until then had been around $80,000. The Disney offer was therefore a life-changing sum by any ordinary measure. Yet his mother understood that the value of the opportunity might extend far beyond what was being offered upfront.Why his mother turned down $2 millionHaywood, who had experience in the music industry as a singer with the Chicago group Kitty & the Haywoods and as a backing vocalist for Aretha Franklin, was not easily swayed by a large cheque. She understood that entertainment contracts could have consequences lasting years, and she wanted her son to benefit if the film continued to generate revenue long after its theatrical release.Her thinking was rooted in Disney's own history. The studio had repeatedly brought its classic animated films back to audiences through re-releases, allowing them to find new generations of viewers. With Aladdin and Beauty and the Beast having already established the commercial strength of Disney's animated revival, she had reason to believe that The Lion King could enjoy a similarly long life.As Weaver explained, his mother looked beyond the immediate payout and considered what the film might mean for him decades later.“She was able to see the playing field and go, wait a minute, this is gonna make a lot of money over time, so what happens when my son turns 40? Is he still gonna be able to get a check from this when they eventually release this?” he recalled. “And sure enough, she was absolutely right.”Instead of accepting the $2 million outright, Haywood negotiated an upfront payment of approximately $100,000 along with royalties. It was a gamble that required patience and a willingness to bet on the film's future success rather than take a guaranteed fortune in the present.The gamble that kept paying off for more than three decadesThe decision was not without risk. Weaver has said that royalty arrangements were not routinely offered to newcomers at the time, with such deals more commonly associated with established stars. His mother's industry experience, however, gave her the confidence to negotiate rather than simply accept Disney's first proposal.The scale of The Lion King's success ultimately made that decision particularly rewarding. What began as an animated feature grew into a global entertainment franchise, spanning merchandise, video games, stage productions, theme park attractions and subsequent screen adaptations.Weaver has pointed to the enormous sums generated by the franchise over the years, observing that the money Disney made from it could run into hundreds of millions, if not billions, of dollars. Against that backdrop, the original $2 million offer began to look less like an extraordinary windfall and more like a one-time payment that could have cost him years of earnings.The actor has said that he has since earned more through the arrangement than the amount Disney initially offered. He has not publicly disclosed the total royalties he has received or the precise amount of his recurring payments, but he continues to describe the income as a welcome source of financial security.In fact, the first royalty cheque was so unexpected that even Weaver and his mother initially questioned whether it was correct.“When I got my first royalty check, me and my mom thought it was a mistake,” he said.That disbelief has given way to appreciation over the years. For Weaver, the payments are a reminder of a decision made when he was too young to fully understand the financial implications of the opportunity in front of him.‘I wasn't thinking about a portfolio’Looking back, Weaver has also acknowledged that receiving $2 million at 13 might not necessarily have led to the same long-term outcome. As a teenager, he was unlikely to have been thinking about investments, financial planning or ways to preserve a fortune over several decades.“I wasn’t thinking about a portfolio, or diversifying,” he said.His mother's decision, therefore, did more than secure a potential stream of future earnings. It also protected him from the possibility of receiving an enormous sum at an age when managing it responsibly would have been a challenge.The continuing royalties have proved particularly valuable because they are not dependent on whether he is currently working on a film, television show or music project. As Weaver put it, the residual income remains helpful even today.“Honestly that income, that residual income that I generate—man that is so helpful,” he said. “Even nowadays, when I get a check, it’s like...yes!”The arrangement also has implications for the next generation. Weaver has said that he agreed to terms allowing the royalties to pass down to his children and potentially their descendants, extending the benefits of his mother's decision well beyond his own career.From young Simba to a career across television, film and musicWhile The Lion King remains one of the defining achievements of Weaver's early career, it was far from his last major professional milestone. After voicing young Simba and singing on the film's soundtrack, he went on to establish himself as an actor in both television and cinema.He appeared in the sitcom Thea from 1993 to 1994 before taking on the role of Marcus Henderson in Smart Guy, which ran from 1997 to 1999. His film credits include Drumline, The Ladykillers and ATL. In more recent years, he has appeared in television series including The Chi and Sistas.Music remained an important part of his journey, too. Weaver released his debut album, Love Ambition, through Motown in 1995. In 2004, he featured on Chingy's single “One Call Away”, which reached No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100.His career has therefore extended well beyond the Disney classic, but the financial benefits of his work on The Lion King continue to occupy a special place in his story.A decision that turned a childhood opportunity into a lasting legacyThe success of The Lion King has only reinforced the wisdom of Haywood's decision. The original animated film became a global box-office phenomenon, while the 2019 photorealistic remake went on to earn more than $1.6 billion worldwide. The franchise's continuing popularity has helped keep the story relevant to new generations of audiences.Online estimates have placed Weaver's net worth between $4 million and $7 million, although those figures have not been independently confirmed. More importantly, the actor himself has made clear that the royalties have continued to provide meaningful financial support throughout his adult life.There is also something deeply personal about the story. At 13, Weaver was the face, or, more accurately, the voice, of a character who would become a beloved part of popular culture. He could not have been expected to predict the franchise's extraordinary longevity. His mother, however, recognised that a successful film could become an enduring asset rather than a single paycheque.More than 30 years later, the result is a reminder that the biggest financial decision is not always about how much money arrives today, but how much value an opportunity can create over time.For Weaver, the $2 million Disney offer might once have seemed like a dream come true. Instead, his mother's willingness to look beyond it helped turn a childhood role into a source of income that continues to surprise him, and one that may benefit his family for generations to come.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Traitors' Celia Imrie and Wiltshire's Fidelis Morgan travel world
articles.summary: Celia Imrie and Wiltshire actress Fedilis Morgan will be talking about their new book at the event.
articles.body:
A Wiltshire writer and actress has said travelling the world with Celebrity Traitors star Celia Imrie is "easy" because they are very well-matched companions.

Fidelis Morgan is not only friends with Imrie but is also collaborating with her on a book called "The Elegant Hustler: Adventures From a Life on the Move". The pair will be discussing it at the Cheltenham Literature Festival.

Imrie, 74 - who has starred in shows from Dinnerladies to the Bridget Jones films and more recently the Celebrity Traitors - said she was "so happy" the "extraordinary" BBC hit series had given her new generations of young fans.

Morgan said Traitors was a "very early lesson in psychology" for young people.

Residents living in 'limbo' after Fairford incident

Man, 72, to crawl across counties after World Cup bet

Dog walker murdered in the woods, say police

The pair, who met in 1975 while working for The Royal Shakespeare Company, said it was there they realised they both "adored travelling" and could have fun together on the way

Imrie said: "The best thing about Fidelis is when things go wrong, she laughs and makes me laugh, and it's heaven."

The pair have been travelling the world by train, ship and plane and documenting their adventures along the way

The duo said it was their preference to travel by sea and rail and avoid flying if possible.

"I had two pulmonary embolisms and the doctor said best not [fly] if you can avoid it and I'm very happy to avoid airports," Imrie said.

Morgan added: "You see things in American trains that you would never see if you drove or if you flew.

"We've seen the wildest of animals - alligators and roadrunners, bears, orange pigs - and eagles."

The pair will make their appearance at the Cheltenham Literature Festival on Friday 16 October.

articles.title: In Mira-Bhayander, BJP and Shiv Sena netas announce plan to raise funds from their Navratri events for drought-hit
articles.summary: BJP and Shiv Sena leaders in Mira-Bhayander pledge Navratri event funds for drought relief: BJP targets Rs 1 crore, Sena plans Rs 7–8 crore via sponsors.
articles.body: Bhayander: The political rivalry between BJP and Shiv Sena in Mira-Bhayander has spilled over into Navratri celebrations, with both parties announcing plans to raise funds for drought-affected people through their respective events.BJP’s Lotus Navratri, organised by the East West Foundation led by MLA Narendra Mehta, will donate proceeds from passes to drought relief. Standing committee chairperson Hasmukh Gehlot said the organisers would provide at least Rs 1 crore for the cause.Following this announcement, state transport minister Pratap Sarnaik has declared that the Navratri festival organised by the Pratap Sarnaik Foundation will be free for all visitors.
